rule: Ground feathers ward lanterns from wraiths
texts: When a Keeper scatters ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths.
Whenever a Keeper spreads ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths.
Wraiths do not approach a warded lantern.
Stale ground feathers do not ward lanterns.

fields.sentence: When a Keeper scatters ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths.
parse: (: whenever_scatter_ward (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $e_scatter scatter) (Agent $e_scatter $k) (GroupOf $f ground_feather) (Theme $e_scatter $f) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l lit) (Around $e_scatter $l)) (And (Member (sk_ward $e_scatter) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $e_scatter) $f) (Theme (sk_ward $e_scatter) $l) (Against (sk_ward $e_scatter) wraith) (During (sk_ward $e_scatter) $e_scatter))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: 'ground feathers' is fused into the compound kind ground_feather (statements 0-1, with the modifier genus (Inheritance ground_feather ground)), but the adjective+noun fusion licence covers only a term of art, nationality/origin adjective, role title or material adjective, and a participial state modifier is none of those — cf. 'a laminated worktop' -> (Member sk_worktop_1 laminated), the split form, which on a plural distributes over the members instead; the modifier genus also falls outside the three exposure categories (gradable / positional-cardinal / material).

review.notes: Around and Against are obliques named after their own prepositions and so licensed. The whenever routing on indefinite participants, 'a Keeper' as a lowercase common-noun kind with no Name atom, 'lit' as its own participial-adjective atom, and the referring-use 'keeper' correctly getting no (can keep) capability are all right.

issues.reason: 'A participle used as a modifier is an adjective' with the split form as its stated example ('a laminated worktop' → (Member … laminated)), and adjective+noun fusion is licensed only for a recognized kind (term of art, nationality/origin, role title, material adjective) and 'never for incidental description' — participial 'ground' is none of those, so fusing ground_feather violates the stated licence.

new_gaps: a descriptively-modified bare plural inside a rule premise ('ground feathers' as a trigger participant) has no licensed form: the mandated split distributes the modifier per member via an assertion-side rule, and a premise cannot carry a per-member property of a variable group
adjudication.defect_summary: The split form is mandated — the group typed (GroupOf $f feather) with 'ground' predicated of each member — but a whenever-premise has no licensed carrier for a per-member property of a variable group, so no fully compliant trigger encoding exists; filed as a gap.
adjudication.notes: The issue's secondary point is weaker — the stated predication test ('the line is part of speech, not meaning') would arguably admit a participial adjective as an exposed genus on a licensed compound — but the fusion bar itself decides the defect.

fields.sentence: Whenever a Keeper spreads ground feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths.
parse: (: keeper_ritual (Implication (Member $k keeper) (And (Member (sk_spread $k) spread) (Agent (sk_spread $k) $k) (Theme (sk_spread $k) (sk_feathers $k)) (GroupOf (sk_feathers $k) ground_feather) (Around (sk_spread $k) (sk_lantern $k)) (Member (sk_lantern $k) lantern) (Member (sk_lantern $k) lit) (Member (sk_shield $k) shield) (Agent (sk_shield $k) (sk_feathers $k)) (Theme (sk_shield $k) (sk_lantern $k)) (Against (sk_shield $k) wraith) (During (sk_shield $k) (sk_spread $k)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The "whenever" trigger clause sits in the CONCLUSION instead of the premises — the only premise is (Member $k keeper), so the rule derives a spreading of ground feathers around a lit lantern for every Keeper, asserting an occurrence the sentence merely conditions on.

(Inheritance ground_feather ground) exposes a modifier genus that the compound rule licenses only for a gradable, positional or material ADJECTIVE modifier — "ground" is either a noun modifier (never exposed) or a participial adjective belonging to none of those three classes.

q2_gaps: a PARTICIPIAL modifier inside a compound kind ("ground feathers") — the fusion list (term of art / nationality / role title / material adjective) and the modifier-genus exposure list (gradable / positional / material adjective) both omit participial adjectives, so neither whether to fuse nor whether to expose the modifier is decided
review.notes: Roles, the two definites resolved back to the trigger's feather group and lantern, the Around / Against preposition-named obliques, the "lit" participial adjective as a separate Member atom, and the During tie are all right. The damage is confined to the premise/conclusion split.

issues.reason: The 'Every time / whenever' rule mandates the trigger clause as the premises and the response as a per-occurrence Skolem consequent, so with (Member $k keeper) as the sole premise the rule derives the spreading, the feather group, the lit lantern and the shielding for every keeper — asserting occurrences the sentence only conditions on.

The noun-modifier half would bar exposure outright, but under the equally available participle-of-grind reading 'ground' is an adjectival property passing the stated predication test, so in territory the gradable/positional/material exposure list genuinely leaves undecided the definitional atom is true and well-typed — acceptable improvisation under the calibration line rather than a second defect.

gaps_confirmed: participial modifier inside a compound kind ('ground feathers'): neither the adjective+noun fusion list (term of art / nationality / role title / material) nor the modifier-genus exposure list (gradable / positional / material) decides participial adjectives, so whether to fuse and whether to expose are both open
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form puts the trigger in the premises with plain variables and Skolemizes the response on the occurrence: (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $s spread) (Agent $s $k) (Theme $s $f) (GroupOf $f ground_feather) (Around $s $l) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l lit)) (And (Member (sk_shield $s) shield) (Agent (sk_shield $s) $f) (Theme (sk_shield $s) $l) (Against (sk_shield $s) wraith) (During (sk_shield $s) $s))) (STV 1.0 0.9), the genus decomposition standing as parsed.
adjudication.notes: Roles, the Around/Against obliques, the definite rebinding and the rule TV are otherwise per the instruction set. The modifier-genus question is better carried as the confirmed gap than as a defect.

fields.sentence: Wraiths do not approach a warded lantern.

q2_gaps: scope of an indefinite object under a negated verbal generic ('Ns do not V a/an N') — the instruction set specifies neither the premise-universal reading used here nor a Skolem-function existential inside the strength-0 conclusion
review.notes: The wide-scope reading chosen is the natural meaning the instruction set asks for, and 'warded' is correctly kept as a participial adjective premise conjunct rather than fused or lemmatized to 'ward'.

parse: (: feather_ward (Implication (And (Member $x feather) (Member $x fresh) (Member $x ground)) (And (Member (sk_ward $x) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $x) $x) (Theme (sk_ward $x) lantern))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: The adjectivally-restricted bare-kind subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route rather than a kind-level relation, the restrictions ride as premise conjuncts, `ground` keeps its participial-modifier surface form, and the inanimate transitive subject stays Agent with the unchanged object as Theme at the empirical-generic 0.9/0.9 with no QuantifierPhrase. Reading "fresh" and "ground" as two coordinate modifiers is a judgment call — a "freshly-ground" adverbial reading has no licensed slot either way.

fields.sentence: Stale ground feathers do not ward lanterns.
parse: (: feathers_no_ward (Implication (And (Member $x feather) (Member $x stale) (Member $x ground)) (And (Member (sk_ward $x) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $x) $x) (Theme (sk_ward $x) lantern))) (STV 0.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The premise conjunct (Member $x ground) exposes a noun modifier as a property of the feather, which the instruction set forbids ("night_shift is not night", "the line is part of speech, not meaning") — a location/association noun modifier should ride inside a fused compound kind (premise (Member $x ground_feather) plus genus (Inheritance ground_feather feather)).

review.notes: The adjectivally-restricted kind subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route over the kind-relation route, at strength 0.0 / confidence 0.9 with no QuantifierPhrase (plain "not"), and "stale" is rightly left unfused as incidental description; the transitive inanimate Agent and the unchanged-object Theme on a bare kind filler also follow the stated tests. The one issue hinges on sense: if "ground" were read as the participle of grind, (Member $x ground) would be licensed as a participial modifier-adjective.

issues.reason: Under the available participle-of-grind reading 'ground' is a participial modifier adjective (Names and casing: a participle used as a modifier is an adjective, not the verb), and an adjectivally-restricted kind subject's restrictions become premise conjuncts (Striking & relational generics), so (Member $x ground) is licensed exactly like (Member $x stale) — nothing in the sentence selects the noun-modifier sense the issue presupposes, and where the set does not decide the sense the true, well-typed premise conjunct is acceptable improvisation.

new_gaps: participial adjective + noun ('ground feathers'): the fusion list (term of art / nationality / role title / material adjective) and the modifier-genus exposure list both omit participial adjectives, and no tiebreaker resolves the participle-of-grind vs noun sense of 'ground', so faithful parses can legitimately differ between the fused-compound and split-modifier treatments
adjudication.notes: The strength-0.0 / confidence-0.9 distributing rule with no QuantifierPhrase, the inanimate transitive Agent, and the bare-kind Theme lantern all follow the stated tests.
